subject: Re: Order schedule — Packaging tiers, stair-step discounts & trigger language (redline request)
messages:
From: Emma Harris <emma.harris@aurelia-analytics.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Lin <tom.lin@aurelia-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Order schedule — packaging tiers & discount triggers (Q3 RFP)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Aurelia is finalizing the procurement packet and we have a couple of callouts in the pricing exhibit that need clarity before legal will take the order form forward:

1) Stair-step discount mapping: The exhibit lists a 5/10/15% step at volume bands but the definition of "aggregate monthly tokens" vs "billable tokens" is ambiguous. Our billing team needs the exact numerator to avoid downstream reconciliation disputes.

2) Packaging tiering and SKU siloing: The RFP assumes we can map three SKUs to the same bundle with prorated credits if we move between SKUs during a quarter. Your draft order schedule looks like it allows this but the clawback language in Section 5 implies an annual true-up only. We need conditional language for mid-quarter SKU migrations.

3) Trigger smoothing and temporary caps: We're comfortable with a soft cap, but we need a defined smoothing window (30/60/90 days) and a maximum catch-up credit so we don't get hit with unpredictable retro invoices.

Attaching our RFP excerpt and examples (Aurelia_RFP_Q3_v2.pdf). Can you provide a marked-up pricing exhibit with proposed wording that addresses the three points above? If you can send by EOD Wednesday we can keep the Q3 procurement window.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if that's easier.

Best,
Emma
Director, Procurement
Aurelia Analytics

Attachment: Aurelia_RFP_Q3_v2.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Harris <emma.harris@aurelia-analytics.com>
Cc: Tom Lin <tom.lin@aurelia-analytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order schedule — packaging tiers & discount triggers (Q3 RFP)

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear notes and for the RFP excerpt. Appreciate the examples; they help a lot.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I attach a proposed redline (RI_redline_v1.docx) that attempts to resolve each of your three bullets.
- We clarified the metric definition to use "billable tokens (per invoice)" and added a short appendix that explains rounding and multi-SKU aggregation rules.
- For SKU migrations mid-quarter, the redline adds a pro-rata migration credit and a capped reconciliation mechanism (Section 5.2).
- For smoothing, we proposed a 60-day smoothing window by default with an opt-out to 30 days for enterprise customers; the maximum retrospective credit is capped at 25% of the month in question.

I copied Karthik and Laura to confirm operational feasibility and Aditya to review the legal language. If legal has strong objections, we can iterate quickly.

Would you be open to a 30-minute call tomorrow (Wed 15 May) at 10:00 am PT to walk through the redline? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and a short one-pager that highlights the three main edits.

Regards,

--
Soojín Lee

On Tue, May 14, 2028 at 11:08 AM Soojín Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> I attach a proposed redline (RI_redline_v1.docx) that attempts to resolve each of your three bullets.

Thanks — skimmed the redline and left a couple of operational notes inline in pricing_exhibit_markup.pdf. High level:
- Confirming we can support multi-SKU proration within a single invoice period; ops will treat SKU migrations as state transitions and apply a prorated credit on the next invoice. We should call out that credits only apply when migrations are between functionally compatible SKUs (same model family).
- The "billable tokens" definition is good, but suggest we add an explicit example table (we should ship this as part of the exhibit) so Aurelia's billing team can reproduce calculations.
- The 25% retrospective cap is acceptable but let's soften the wording around "retroactive invoicing" to make sure we preserve our right to true-up over a 12-month window for abuse/chargeback events.

I attached markup: pricing_exhibit_markup.pdf. If legal is comfortable we should propose the call to the customer and try to lock this during the week.

—Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Harris <emma.harris@aurelia-analytics.com>, Tom Lin <tom.lin@aurelia-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order schedule — packaging tiers, stair-step reconciliation & smoothing (final)

Emma / Tom —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Based on Aurelia's asks and our internal review, here's what we're proposing as the final exhibit updates (summary):

1) Metric clarity: "Billable tokens" will be defined as the total tokens invoiced per billing period after known pre-billing discounts and excluding tokens covered by explicit free-tier credits. See Exhibit A, Table 1 for worked examples.

2) SKU migration: Added Section 5.2 — prorated migration credit effective on the next invoice; applies only between SKUs in the same model family (we listed examples). Migration credits are time-limited and cannot be stacked with promotional credits.

3) Smoothing & caps: Default smoothing window set to 60 days; customer may request 30 days in writing. Retro credit cap set at 25% of affected month; Redwood reserves a 12-month true-up right for exceptional reconciliation, fraud, or chargeback scenarios.

We've attached the consolidated redline and an appendix with two calculation examples. If that language looks good to you, we'll prepare the final order form for signature and include a short CSV export template for your billing team to use during onboarding.

Proposed next step: 30-min call tomorrow, Thu May 16 at 9:00 am PT to run the examples and confirm the CSV template. Let me know if you prefer another time and I'll update the invite.

Appreciate the partnership here — hoping we can close this week so onboarding can start in June.

Best,

--
Soojín Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
